title: Observation of room temperature intrinsic nonlinear thermoelectric effects in low-dimensional semimetals
authors: Kurea Nakagawa, Krishnaraajan Sundararajan, Cédric A. Cordero-Silis, Bart J. van Wees, Marcos H. D. Guimarães
abstract: Nonreciprocal control of thermoelectric responses offers a promising strategy for next-generation thermal-management and energy-conversion. While nonlinear electrical transport has recently emerged as an intrinsic property of low-symmetry quantum materials, their thermoelectric counterparts have not been demonstrated. Here, exploiting harmonic detection with gradient-reversal techniques, we report intrinsic nonlinear thermoelectric responses up to room temperature in the low-symmetry type-II Weyl semimetals $T_\mathrm{d}$-WTe$_2$ and TaIrTe$_4$ in the absence of magnetic fields or magnetic materials. We resolve all symmetry-allowed components of the second-order thermoelectric tensor, including the nonlinear Seebeck, nonlinear Nernst, and nonlinear mixed-directional thermoelectric effects and demonstrate that both Berry-curvature-related and scattering-induced contributions govern the different nonlinear thermoelectric responses. Our results show that nonlinear thermoelectricity arises intrinsically from reduced crystal symmetry and that engineering effects related to scattering in these materials provides a versatile platform for exploring higher-order heat-to-charge current conversion beyond the linear response.
summary: This work reports the first observation of intrinsic nonlinear thermoelectric effects—including NLS, NLN, and NLMT—at room temperature in low-symmetry Weyl semimetals. By employing harmonic detection techniques, the authors successfully isolated these higher-order responses, demonstrating that they arise fundamentally from reduced crystal symmetry rather than external magnetic fields.
main_problem: The study aims to demonstrate and characterize intrinsic nonlinear thermoelectric effects at room temperature in low-dimensional semimetals, moving beyond reliance on external symmetry breaking.
main_result: All three symmetry-allowed components of the nonlinear thermoelectric tensor (NLS, NLN, NLMT) were observed intrinsically up to room temperature in $	ext{WTe}_2$ and $	ext{TaIrTe}_4$.
method: Measurements utilized harmonic detection ($4\omega$) techniques on fabricated devices with specific geometries to isolate intrinsic nonlinear contributions from linear response terms.
model_or_system: The physical systems are low-symmetry type-II Weyl semimetals ($	ext{WTe}_2$ and $	ext{TaIrTe}_4}$). The analysis uses a third-rank tensor formalism ($\mathbf{S}^{(2)}$) to describe the nonlinear thermoelectric response.
key_observables: Nonlinear Seebeck (NLS), Nonlinear Nernst (NLN), and Nonlinear Mixed-directional thermoelectric (NLMT) coefficients, measured as fourth-harmonic voltage responses ($E_{i, 4\omega}$).
important_parameters: Room temperature ($\sim 290 	ext{K}$); zero magnetic field; low-dimensional semimetals.
main_assumptions: The intrinsic nonlinear contribution is isolated by exploiting the directional nature of linear effects through symmetrization and ruling out temperature dependence of heater resistance.
figures_summary: Figures show device schematics, measured fourth-harmonic responses for NLS/NLMT/NLN in $	ext{TaIrTe}_4$, and the temperature dependence of these nonlinear coefficients in both materials.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework using second-order tensors for linear response and third-rank tensors for nonlinear effects. It details experimental measurements using harmonic detection to isolate intrinsic contributions, followed by analysis showing the origin (Berry curvature vs. scattering) and temperature dependence of these novel thermoelectric responses.
why_interesting: While focused on solid-state transport, the ability to engineer higher-order energy conversion mechanisms via symmetry control is relevant for understanding non-equilibrium quantum dynamics in mesoscopic systems.
